question: Which of the following rocks is formed by the cooling and crystallisation of magma?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Granite**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On all continents, **granitic rocks** can be found close to or past plate borders.
 
• They developed as **magma** **cooled thousands of kilometres below the surface of the Earth.**
 
• Then, as the** volcanic mountains** above them eroded away, the **granitic rocks** were elevated to the surface.
 
• **Granitic rocks**, which were cooled from rock melted during the subduction process that also created the **Franciscan Complex's rocks**, make up the **Sierra Nevada's core in California.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Magma**

 
 
• All **igneous rocks **are formed from **magma**, which is a naturally occurring substance that is molten or semi-molten.
 
• The **Earth** possesses **magma** beneath its surface, and other terrestrial planets and several naturally occurring satellites have also been confirmed to have magmatic activity.
 
• **Magma** may also include gas bubbles and suspended crystals in addition to molten rock.
 
• In a variety o**f tectonic settings on Earth,** including as subduction **zones**, continental rift **zones**, mid-ocean ridges, and hotspots, the **mantle** or the **crust** melts to produce **magma**.
 
• **Mantle and crustal melts** are assumed to be stored in **magma** **chambers** **or trans-crustal crystal-rich **mush zones as they move upward through the **crust**.
